overview: Brent crude surged to a five-month high near $111.75 on Tuesday before settling at $110.17, driven by fresh attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. Reuters reported at least 18 vessel attacks over the past two weeks, and Iran's IRGC warned it could extend restrictions to the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and the Suez Canal. The IEA's October Oil Market Report puts Hormuz crude flows at 10.9 million barrels a day — roughly 80% of the pre-war baseline — but cautioned that energy markets will not return to normal next year. Pakistan is mediating a ceasefire proposal that both sides are reportedly reviewing. Coal held near $150.70, up over 40% year-to-date.

Gold slipped 0.6% to $4,117 as US Treasury yields remained elevated near 5.2% ahead of the October 27–28 FOMC meeting. Silver was a standout, rising 1.7% to $57.92 on industrial demand. Grains extended their losses: December corn fell 5 cents to $4.62, wheat dropped 12 cents to $6.43, and soybeans slipped 5¼ cents to $12.48 on harvest pressure. Bitcoin fell below $82,000 to $81,400 amid persistent ETF outflows, while Ethereum held near $2,440. Tesla, Meta, Netflix and Lam Research report earnings this week.

watchItems.title: Hormuz attacks hit wartime high
watchItems.text: Reuters reports at least 18 vessel attacks over the past two weeks, including Iran claiming two tankers struck by naval mines. Iran's IRGC warned it could extend restrictions to the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and the Suez Canal. Brent touched a five-month high above $111. Pakistan is mediating a ceasefire proposal both sides are reviewing.

watchItems.title: FOMC, Oct 27–28
watchItems.text: The Fed remains in its communications blackout. Markets see less than 20% chance of an October hike, but September CPI at 3.7% y/y and the 10-year yield above 5.2% keep the door open. Statement language will drive gold, silver and rate-sensitive assets.

watchItems.title: Big-cap earnings: Tesla, Meta, Netflix
watchItems.text: Tesla and Meta report Wednesday, Netflix Thursday. Energy costs and AI capex are key margin drivers across sectors. The Nasdaq is testing its recent lows after a 4.5% decline the prior week.

watchItems.title: IEA: no return to normal next year
watchItems.text: The IEA's October Oil Market Report warned that energy markets will not normalize in 2027 as long as Hormuz disruptions persist. Crude flows are at about 80% of pre-war levels, and refined-product shipments — especially diesel and jet fuel — remain severely constrained.

desk.name: Gold
desk.sum: Gold slipped 0.6% to about $4,117 on Tuesday as US Treasury yields held near 5.2% and the dollar remained firm ahead of the October 27–28 FOMC meeting. Markets are pricing less than 20% odds of an October rate move, but September CPI at 3.7% y/y keeps the door open. Gold remains about 27% below its January record near $5,608.

desk.name: Silver
desk.sum: Silver rallied 1.7% to $57.92 on Tuesday, outperforming gold on renewed industrial demand. The metal is down about 12% on the month but the Silver Institute projects a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit, providing a floor under prices. Silver remains about 52% below its late-January record near $121.6.

desk.name: Oil
desk.sum: Brent crude rose to a five-month high near $111.75 on Tuesday before settling at $110.17, after Reuters reported at least 18 tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz over the past two weeks. Iran claimed two tankers were struck by naval mines and the IRGC warned it could extend restrictions to the Bab al-Mandeb and Suez Canal. The IEA cautioned that energy markets will not return to normal next year. WTI settled near $99.

desk.name: Copper
desk.sum: Copper firmed to $6.57 per pound on Tuesday, supported by tight mine supply and ongoing Chile disruptions. BHP reported a 19% drop in September-quarter copper output to 400,700 tonnes. The metal is down 1.7% on the month but remains near record territory, trading about 4% below its September high of $6.85.

desk.name: Coal
desk.sum: Newcastle coal edged up to $150.70 a tonne, holding near a three-year high. The IEA expects global coal demand to rise 1.2% to a record 8.94 billion tonnes this year as the Hormuz gas shock continues to drive Asian and European utilities back to coal. Coal is up over 40% year-to-date, supported by Indonesia's tightened export rules and an Australian court ruling blocking a NSW mine expansion.

desk.name: Platinum
desk.sum: Platinum rose 1.5% to $1,660 on Tuesday, continuing its recovery from a three-month low hit last week. Industrial demand expectations are firming, though the WPIC still forecasts an 18% drop in total platinum demand this year. The metal remains about 7.9% below its September levels.

desk.name: Palladium
desk.sum: Palladium edged up to $1,106 but remains in a steep downtrend, now roughly 16% below its September levels and more than 25% lower on the year. EV adoption continues to erode catalytic-converter demand, and Russia's sanctions waiver could ease tight supply from Norilsk Nickel, adding a bearish overhang.

desk.name: Hormuz Terminal
desk.sum: The Strait of Hormuz crisis escalated further, with Reuters reporting at least 18 vessel attacks over the past two weeks, including Iran claiming two tankers struck by naval mines. The IEA's October report puts crude flows at 10.9 million barrels a day, roughly 80% of the pre-war baseline. Iran's IRGC warned it could extend restrictions to the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and the Suez Canal, while Houthis claimed strikes on Saudi Aramco facilities in Yanbu and the Shaybah oilfield. Pakistan is mediating a ceasefire proposal both sides are reviewing.

desk.name: Corn
desk.sum: December corn fell 5 cents to $4.62 on Tuesday as harvest pressure intensified. The corn harvest reached 44% complete, behind the five-year average of 52%, but dry forecasts are accelerating fieldwork. Corn is now down about 15% on the month as fund liquidation continues.

desk.name: Wheat
desk.sum: CBOT December wheat dropped 12 cents to $6.43 on Tuesday, the sharpest one-day loss in two weeks. Winter wheat planting reached 63%, behind the five-year average of 69%, and weak export demand is compounding the selling pressure. Wheat is down about 12% on the month but remains more than 30% higher year-to-date.

desk.name: Soybean
desk.sum: November soybeans fell 5¼ cents to $12.48 on Tuesday, weighed down by harvest pressure and technical selling. Traders largely ignored a 22.5 million bushel sale to China. The US soybean harvest continues to run ahead of the five-year average and is pointing to a record crop.

desk.name: Cryptocurrencies
desk.sum: Bitcoin fell 1.9% to about $81,400 on Tuesday, dropping below the key $82,000 support level that has now flipped to resistance. US spot bitcoin ETFs have seen about $910 million in net outflows in October. Ethereum edged up to about $2,440. Markets are cautious ahead of the FOMC's October 27–28 meeting and this week's earnings from Tesla, Meta and Netflix.
